### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via lookupFilters (literal, a string literal in FIELD_NAME_SLOTS))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via lookupFilters (literal, a string literal in FIELD_NAME_SLOTS))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx`  _(via lookupFilters (literal, a string literal in FIELD_NAME_SLOTS))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx`  _(via lookupFilters (literal, a string literal in FIELD_NAME_SLOTS))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/relationships.mdx`  _(via lookupFilters (literal, a string literal in FIELD_NAME_SLOTS))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx`  _(via lookupFilters (literal, a string literal in FIELD_NAME_SLOTS))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/schema.mdx`  _(via lookupFilters (literal, a string literal in FIELD_NAME_SLOTS))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via lookupFilters (literal, a string literal in FIELD_NAME_SLOTS))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via lookupFilters (literal, a string literal in FIELD_NAME_SLOTS))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via lookupFilters (literal, a string literal in FIELD_NAME_SLOTS))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via lookupFilters (literal, a string literal in FIELD_NAME_SLOTS))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 43dd5656e47001bf26ba5b441683ae836aebf816` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `37793cd5f8b05c68fcee0c3dfedbe3ef65ef3338` — the merge of head `99ff6598430c8b3e00cc6691e22ce09d3527de04` into base `43dd5656e47001bf26ba5b441683ae836aebf816`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 37793cd5f8b05c68fcee0c3dfedbe3ef65ef3338 && git checkout 37793cd5f8b05c68fcee0c3dfedbe3ef65ef3338
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 43dd5656e47001bf26ba5b441683ae836aebf816 99ff6598430c8b3e00cc6691e22ce09d3527de04 && git checkout -B drift-repro 43dd5656e47001bf26ba5b441683ae836aebf816 && git merge --no-ff 99ff6598430c8b3e00cc6691e22ce09d3527de04

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 43dd5656e47001bf26ba5b441683ae836aebf816
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 43dd5656e47001bf26ba5b441683ae836aebf816` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The rule `object-field-ref-unknown` gains a `lookupFilters[].value.$record` member in its owner-addressed sweep. It applies to picker field types only and follows at most one hop. It comes with an ADR-0087 semantic entry `lookup-filter-record-path-unknown-refused` and a changeset (lint + spec minor, `feat(lint)!`). Declarations: `Clause-②: no` (narrowing), `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`.

The seat has read the dev's deviations:

2. N7 (a nested `$record`) is left unnamed and pinned.
3. List members are not read, because the parse already refuses them.

Main is not merged (K small; #34132 has no overlap). The seat merges at landing if K ≥ 15.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d180955e532ba29062b92d2ac11a024151b802ab`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.lookup-filter-record-path-unknown-refused.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.test.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, .changeset/34200-lookup-filter-record-path-checked.md

Read at 2026-11-16T02:50Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6905524732; lane request 6905509101 on mailbox #33873. Independence: implemented in an os-steve project thread, dispatched by domain:spec#2 (os-steve); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

No prior record for this PR; findings are numbered fresh and continue no earlier id. Read, not reviewed (outside the diff, at this head): `packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts` (`resolveFieldPath`, `RELATIONSHIP_FIELD_TYPES`, `indexServedObjectGraph`, `describeFieldPathVerdict`), `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` (`LookupFilterRecordReferenceSchema`, `LOOKUP_FILTER_RECORD_PATH_RE`, `refuseMalformedLookupFilterEntry`), `packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts` (`REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES`, `referenceTargetOf`), `packages/lint/src/reference-integrity-suite.ts`, `packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts`, the sibling entries `18.lookup-filter-record-reference-shape-refused.ts` and `18.object-field-pointer-unknown-refused.ts`, and AGENTS.md on `origin/main`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **What is refused is what the declaration already excludes.** The new member resolves the path with the family's `resolveFieldPath` against the object that owns the picker field, on the served graph (object extensions folded in). It refuses four shapes: a head that is no field of that object, a hop through a field that is not a relationship, a leaf the referenced object lacks, and a path of more than one hop. The published contract on `main` (`LookupFilterRecordReferenceSchema` and its describe) says the path is a field of the record being edited or one lookup hop from it, and two hops are refused at parse. So the lint makes the spec's own sentence real; it takes no declared capability away.
- **No reader exists to compare against.** At this head nothing under `ui/` or `packages/` resolves a `lookupFilters` `{ $record }` (the picker reader is #34197; both describes carry `[PLANNED — not enforced]`). "Exactly what the runtime resolves" can therefore only be judged against the declaration, and the diff says so in its own module table ("judged as declared"). When #34197 lands, its resolver and this slot must agree; that is #34197's acceptance, not a defect here.
- **Over-narrowing cases, each read in the cited code:**
  - A registry-injected column as a single name (`created_at`, `id`, `owner_id` on an owned object) resolves: the leaf test reads the authored names and then the injected map. Pinned for `created_at`.
  - A hop through an injected column (`owner_id.name`) is `unknowable` and never reported.
  - A formula or summary field is an authored field and resolves as any other.
  - A field an object extension contributes resolves at the build, because the graph is the served one.
  - A hop to an object outside the stack, to an object with no readable field map, or through a relationship field with no target is not judged. Pinned for the first.
  - There is no polymorphic reference to consider: `reference` is one string and `referenceTargetOf` is the single arbiter.
  - Case: the parse admits lower snake_case only, so no accepted spelling is refused for case.
  - `_id` is admitted by the path regex and is refused here as an unknown field; no object declares or injects that name, so the refusal is correct.
- **Deviation 1 (hop types: lookup, master_detail, user, tree) — accepted, keep it.** The traversable set is the same four types `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES` in the spec defines as "a record id in stored form, the related record in expanded form". A `user` field is declared a lookup to `sys_user`, a `tree` a self-reference. Narrowing the slot to lookup and master_detail would refuse a path the declaration covers, which would be the over-narrowing must-fix. One resolver, one answer.
- **Deviation 2 (a `$record` nested inside a literal is not named) — accepted.** The parse treats it as an opaque literal, nothing reads it, and the rule has no advisory tier. Pinned.
- **Deviation 3 (list members are not read) — accepted.** `refuseMalformedLookupFilterEntry` refuses a `$record` list member on every parsed path; the test pins both halves. On the raw `os lint` path that shape is silent, which `os validate` and the doors close.
- **Deviation 4 (main not merged) — no objection.** The entry id is absent from `origin/main` and distinct from its #34009 sibling; the seat merges at landing.
- **Doors.** The rule is a member of the reference-integrity suite with `runtimeTypes: ['flow', 'object']`, so it runs at the CLI commands and at the runtime authoring gate on an object write. The declaration names `os lint`, `os validate`, `os build` and the runtime publish door; the semantic entry lists the metadata doors in the same words as `18.object-field-pointer-unknown-refused`, the family's existing entry. The runtime gate is differential: a stored object that already carries such a path is not charged on a later write that does not add it, so no stored row starts failing a save it did not cause.
- **Interaction with #34078.** No contradiction and no double verdict on one door. On a parsed path a two-hop or non-snake_case path stops at the parse; the lint's own two-hop sentence is reached only on the raw `os lint` path, and says the same thing. A `$record` miss and the same entry's `.field` miss are two findings on purpose (two objects, two fixes) and are pinned as two.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the correct arm: the diff refuses what parsed before and admits nothing new (`yes (narrowing)` is the mixed widen-and-narrow reading, which this is not). Line-initial in the PR body and the changeset body.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is correct (a value refused). The kind takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves: `@objectstack/lint` minor and `@objectstack/spec` minor, both moved. Correct.
- BREAKING: the title carries `!`, the changeset carries the `**BREAKING**` banner, the FROM and TO, the one-line fix, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`registered lookup-filter-record-path-unknown-refused`).
- The semantic entry is well-formed against `SemanticMigration`: id kebab-case and unique under `semantic/18.*`, surface, replacement, reason, acceptance criteria. No D2 conversion is right (which field a misspelt path meant is the author's). `relevantWhen` is optional and omitted, as on the family's sibling entry; not required.
- CI at this head when read: 44 check-runs — 17 success, 10 skipped, 17 still in progress (Test Core 1–8, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, the Type Check jobs and three Lint jobs), none failed. ⛔ This PASS is on the contract; the seat waits for those 17 to finish green before landing. The lane's ADR-0087 registration gate was last run locally one wording-only commit earlier, so the CI run of it at this head is the one that counts.
- CI completed before posting: 67 check-runs on this head, 56 success, 11 skipped, none failed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Only `packages/lint` and one `packages/spec` migration entry move; no schema, no generated artifact, no `ui/` file. The spec describes are untouched and still read `[PLANNED — not enforced]` for the picker, which stays true: this PR enforces the path at authoring, not the picker's resolution.
- Fields that an `objectExtensions` entry contributes are not swept by this field-level loop (it walks each object's own `fields`), for this slot as for every other slot of the family. That is the family's existing limit, not introduced here; the entry's surface names `objects[].fields` only, which matches.
- The publish probe in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts` re-reads each published object through the same rule over that one object and reports without refusing. A stored `$record` miss on the head segment will now appear on that receipt. The declaration does not name the receipt; see N3.
- `lookupFilters` on action and bulk-action params is a different carrier and is not judged here; out of the card's scope.

### ④ Design judgment

**`18.lookup-filter-record-path-unknown-refused.ts`** — holds against the code it cites. The four refused shapes it lists are the four the slot refuses; "a hop to an object outside the stack is not judged" matches `isUnjudgeable`; the remedy (fix the segment; a candidate-row column is a `$field` comparand) matches the spec's own distinction between the two comparands; the measured zero first-party exposure agrees with a search of this head (the only `lookupFilters` `$record` objects are the #34009 fixtures and changeset).

**`validate-object-field-refs.ts`** — agrees with the contract it implements. `pickerOnly` gates on the same three picker types as the rest of the module; the hop bound is applied before resolution; `ownFinding` keeps the `$record` finding out of the `dependsOn` fold in both directions.

**`rule-explanations.ts`** — true and consistent with the message: it says the picker "is declared to" swap the value, which is the honest tense while the reader is unlanded, and names the same four misses.

S1 (should-fix) — The pins cover each refused shape and three accepted ones (single field, injected single column, one hop through a `lookup`), but not the accepted edges the PR's own text asserts for this slot: a hop through a `user` field (the one open design call, deviation 1), a hop through a `tree` field, and a hop through an injected column (`owner_id.x`, stated as unjudged in the PR body). The shared resolver is pinned elsewhere, but a later slot-level hop-type set (the lane's own "option B, a one-line change") would redden nothing in this block. Add one accepted case per edge so the decision the seat is being asked to keep is held by a test.

N1 (nit) — The hint and the two-hop message say "one lookup field" and "one lookup hop" while the slot traverses `user` and `tree` fields too; the explanation says "relationship field". The spec uses "lookup hop" loosely in the same way, so this is wording only.

N2 (nit) — `maxHops` is a general number but its message hard-codes "takes a second hop" and "at most one lookup hop"; and on the raw `os lint` path a malformed path with an empty segment (`a..b`) is reported as a second hop at an empty name. Neither changes a verdict.

N3 (nit) — The changeset could name the publish receipt as a place the finding now appears (reported there, never refused), beside the four doors it lists.

No must-fix.

Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qibxTeW8xHnxoHxWNHWW`

**VERDICT: PASS**

review#2 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibxTeW8xHnxoHxWNHWW

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c83d11952d4f7e2eaec92308b91cbaf17aaaf61e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.lookup-filter-record-path-unknown-refused.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.test.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, .changeset/34200-lookup-filter-record-path-checked.md

Read at 2026-11-16T03:46Z. Delta review of this head against PASS 6905932695 at d180955e; claim: comment 6906660590; lane request 6906637305 on mailbox #33873. Independence: implemented in an os-steve project thread, dispatched by domain:spec#2 (os-steve); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

One commit since `d180955e`: `c83d11952` (4 files, +30/−11) — three tests, wording in one message, one hint, one explanation and two comments, and one changeset clause plus one parenthesis. The semantic entry is byte-identical to the head already passed. Everything the prior record judged in ①–④ and that this commit does not touch stands as written there. Read, not reviewed (outside the diff, at this head): `packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts` (`RELATIONSHIP_FIELD_TYPES`, `graphFieldOf`, `resolveFieldPath`), `packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` and `field.test.ts` (the parse-side wording).

Prior findings, by id:

- **S1 (pins for the accepted edges) — closed.** Three accepted cases added, each read against the fixture and the resolver:
  - `tree`: the fixture's `parent_quote` is `{ type: 'tree', reference: 'sales_quote' }` and the path `parent_quote.quote_date` resolves to a field the object authors, so the verdict is a real `ok`, not a skip. The resolver tests the hop's type before anything else, so a hop set without `tree` answers `hop-not-relationship` and the case reddens.
  - `user`: `approver_user` is `{ type: 'user' }` with no carrier; its target is the type's constant, absent from this stack, so the path is unjudged past the hop — and the title says so. The type test still precedes the target, so a hop set without `user` reddens this case too. Not vacuous.
  - injected column: `owner_id.anything` reaches the resolver's injected-hop skip; were `owner_id` not injected on the fixture object the head would be an unknown field and the case would be red, so green CI is the evidence the edge is the one claimed. This pin holds "not refused", which is the statement the PR makes; a narrower hop-type set would not touch it (the column is a lookup), and nothing claims it would.
- **N1 (lookup field / lookup hop wording) — closed for the lint door.** The two-hop message, the hint and the explanation now say "relationship"; the test that pins the message and the explanation's one-line pin moved in the same commit. No other user-facing string of this slot says "lookup hop" or "lookup field" at this head (searched `packages/`, `content/docs/`, `skills/`, `.changeset/`): the remaining hits are the spec's parse message and describes for `{ $record }` (and the reference docs generated from them, and the #34009 changeset), which this PR does not touch and which `field.test.ts` pins on the spec side. No test or doc elsewhere pinned the old lint strings. The semantic entry already said "relationship field".
- **N2 (general `maxHops`, message hard-codes "second hop"; an empty segment reads as a second hop on the raw path) — open, unchanged.** Carried below as N1.
- **N3 (name the publish receipt) — closed in the changeset.** The clause "reported (never refused) on the package publish receipt's object probe" is true of `build-probes.ts`: the probe re-reads each published object through this rule after the publish and reports. The added parenthesis (`lookup`, `master_detail`, `user` or `tree`) equals `RELATIONSHIP_FIELD_TYPES`. The PR body's line was not given the same clause; see N2.

### ① Derived judgments

- No behaviour moves in this commit. The non-test source edits are text: one message, one hint, one explanation sentence, two comments. What is refused and what is accepted at this head is exactly what was judged at `d180955e`.
- The hop-type decision the seat was asked to keep (lookup, master_detail, user, tree — the spec's own reference value types) is now held by tests in this slot's block, one per non-lookup edge.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged and still correct: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `@objectstack/lint` minor and `@objectstack/spec` minor, the `!` title, the `**BREAKING**` banner and exactly one ADR-0087 marker. The changeset's two edits add a true clause and a true enumeration; neither changes the level or the kind.
- A message string and a hint string changed between two unreleased commits of the same PR; nothing published carried the old wording.
- CI at this head when read: 71 check-runs, all completed — 58 success, 13 skipped, none failed, none running. Test Core 1–8, Lint and Repo Gates, the Type Check jobs and both Check Changeset runs are green.

CI completed before posting: 71 check-runs on this head, 58 success, 13 skipped, none failed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The lint door now says "relationship hop" where the parse door (`LookupFilterRecordReferenceSchema`, outside this diff) still says "lookup hop" for the same bound. Both are true of the same four types; aligning the spec's sentence is a schema-face change and not this PR's to make. Worth a line on #34197 or #34201 so the picker's docs pick one word.
- Nothing else new. The prior record's flags (extension-contributed fields not swept by this loop, the action-param carrier out of scope) are untouched.

### ④ Design judgment

**`18.lookup-filter-record-path-unknown-refused.ts`** — unchanged since the head already passed; still holds against the code it cites, and its "relationship field" wording is now the wording of the message it announces.

**`validate-object-field-refs.ts`** — message and hint agree with the resolver they sit on: the hop is any of the four relationship types, and they say so.

**`validate-object-field-refs.test.ts`** — the three new cases exercise the edges they name (see S1 above). The `user` case stops at the hop because its target is not in the fixture stack; that is the common authoring situation and the title states it.

**`rule-explanations.ts`** — "at most one relationship hop" is consistent with the message and with the sentence that follows it.

**`.changeset/34200-lookup-filter-record-path-checked.md`** — both additions are true as read in the cited code.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
